records.title: FORM 10-Q
records.text: •Net sales for the three months ended March 31, 2024 increased by 45% to $794.1 million compared to $548.3 million for the same period in 2023.

records.title: FORM 10-Q
records.text: Although module average selling prices in many global markets have declined, near-term module pricing in the United States, our primary market, remains relatively stable due, in part, to the rising demand for domestically manufactured modules as a result of the IRA.

records.title: FORM 10-Q
records.text: •As of March 31, 2024, our total installed nameplate production capacity across all our facilities was approximately 17.6 GW.

records.title: FORM 10-Q
records.text: The increase in gross profit was primarily due to the recognition of the advanced manufacturing production credit under Section 45X of the IRC, reductions in sales freight costs, and a higher average selling price per watt for modules sold in the current period.

records.title: FORM 10-Q
records.text: The increase in net cash provided by operating activities was primarily driven by proceeds from sale of Section 45X credits and higher cash receipts from module sales in current period, partially offset by lower advance payments received for future module sales and increased payments made to suppliers in the current period.
